advances:
This proves a conditional root left-tail closure and reduces every remaining failure to explicit residual inequalities. If \(c_j+m<t\) and both other low sets are nonempty, then, with
\[
\Delta_j:=2t-k+c_j,
\]
one necessarily has either \(\Delta_j\ge m\), or the two strict inequalities
\[
c_j>\frac14\left(\sqrt M+\sqrt{m-\Delta_j}\right)^2,
\qquad
4mc_j>M(m-\Delta_j).
\]
Consequently, whenever \(\Delta_j<m\) and either displayed reverse weak inequality holds, at least one of the other two low sets is empty. The proof uses the shared three-direction geometry and compatibility, not separate optimization of the three marginals. The surviving regimes are exactly \(\Delta_j\ge m\), where the small-endpoint simultaneous complement may be empty and this bridge supplies no positive area, and \(\Delta_j<m\) with both displayed strict inequalities.
author: mp_r60_root_left_tail
proof:
Because the three planar bodies are sections of one compact convex polytope, convexity gives
\[
\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}\subseteq K.
\tag{5}
\]
This is also the compatibility implication used in accepted fact `d7bdfc054d5093e8`.

Choose arbitrary
\[
a_i\in I_i,\qquad a_\ell\in I_\ell,
\]
and abbreviate
\[
u_r=F_{0r}(a_r),\qquad v_r=F_{2r}(-a_r)
\qquad(r=i,\ell).
\tag{6}
\]
The two strict low-mass inequalities are
\[
u_i+v_i+c_i<t,\qquad
u_\ell+v_\ell+c_\ell<t.
\tag{7}
\]

Every point of \(K\cap\{f_j>0\}\) belongs to
\[
\{f_i\leq0\}\cup\{f_\ell\leq0\},
\]
because
\[
f_i+f_\ell=-1-f_j<0.
\]
The three cutting lines have planar area zero. Therefore
\[
k-c_j\leq c_i+c_\ell.
\tag{8}
\]
Adding (7) and using (8) gives
\[
u_i+u_\ell+v_i+v_\ell
<2t-c_i-c_\ell
\leq2t-k+c_j
=\Delta_j.
\tag{9}
\]
The left side is nonnegative, so \(\Delta_j>0\).

Put
\[
E_0=A_0\cap\{f_i>a_i,\ f_\ell>a_\ell\},
\qquad
E_2=A_2\cap\{f_i>-a_i,\ f_\ell>-a_\ell\}.
\tag{10}
\]
The union bound gives
\[
|E_0|\geq M-u_i-u_\ell,\qquad
|E_2|\geq m-v_i-v_\ell.
\tag{11}
\]
Assume from now on that \(\Delta_j<m\). By (9), both right sides in (11) are strictly positive.

For \(x_0\in E_0\) and \(x_2\in E_2\), affinity gives
\[
2f_i\left(\frac{x_0+x_2}{2}\right)
=f_i(x_0)+f_i(x_2)>a_i-a_i=0
\]
and likewise
\[
2f_\ell\left(\frac{x_0+x_2}{2}\right)>0.
\]
Equation (5) puts the midpoint in \(K\), while
\[
f_j=-1-f_i-f_\ell<-1
\]
at that midpoint. Hence
\[
\frac{E_0+E_2}{2}
\subseteq
K\cap\{f_j\leq0,\ f_i>0,\ f_\ell>0\}.
\tag{12}
\]
The sets in (10) are measurable and convex and have positive area. The planar Brunn-Minkowski inequality recorded and used in accepted fact `d7bdfc054d5093e8`, applied directly to (12), yields
\[
\sqrt{c_j}
\geq
\frac{\sqrt{|E_0|}+\sqrt{|E_2|}}2
\geq
\frac{
\sqrt{M-u_i-u_\ell}+
\sqrt{m-v_i-v_\ell}
}{2}.
\tag{13}
\]

Set
\[
A=u_i+u_\ell,\qquad B=v_i+v_\ell,\qquad R=A+B.
\]
Then \(0\leq R<\Delta_j<m\). For fixed \(R\), the concave function
\[
A\longmapsto
\sqrt{M-A}+\sqrt{m-(R-A)}
\qquad(0\leq A\leq R)
\]
attains its minimum at an endpoint. The endpoint obtained by taking \(A=0\) is the smaller one, because
\[
\sqrt m-\sqrt{m-R}
\geq
\sqrt M-\sqrt{M-R}
\]
when \(M>m\). Consequently,
\[
\sqrt{M-A}+\sqrt{m-B}
\geq
\sqrt M+\sqrt{m-R}
>
\sqrt M+\sqrt{m-\Delta_j}.
\tag{14}
\]
Combining (13) and (14) proves (3).

There is also a product version which does not discard the common-pair information. Let
\[
\mathcal D_j=
\{(x_0,x_2)\in A_0\times A_2:
f_j(x_0)+f_j(x_2)<0\},
\qquad d_j=|\mathcal D_j|.
\tag{15}
\]
The calculation preceding (12) actually proves
\[
E_0\times E_2\subseteq\mathcal D_j.
\]
Thus
\[
d_j\geq|E_0||E_2|
\geq(M-A)(m-B).
\tag{16}
\]

On the other hand, write \(C_j=K\cap\{f_j<0\}\), whose area is \(c_j\). Under the sum map \(y=x_0+x_2\), Fubini gives
\[
d_j
=
\int_{2C_j}
(\mathbf 1_{A_0}*\mathbf 1_{A_2})(y)\,dy.
\tag{17}
\]
For every \(y\),
\[
(\mathbf 1_{A_0}*\mathbf 1_{A_2})(y)
=|A_0\cap(y-A_2)|
\leq|A_2|=m.
\]
Since \(|2C_j|=4c_j\), equation (17) gives
\[
d_j\leq4mc_j.
\tag{18}
\]

For fixed \(R=A+B<m\), the product
\[
(M-A)(m-(R-A))
\]
is concave in \(A\in[0,R]\), so its minimum is at an endpoint. The value at \(A=0\) is the smaller endpoint value because
\[
(M-R)m-M(m-R)=R(M-m)>0.
\]
Therefore, using \(R<\Delta_j\),
\[
(M-A)(m-B)
\geq M(m-R)
>M(m-\Delta_j).
\tag{19}
\]
Equations (16), (18), and (19) prove (4).

The final equivalent formulation is the contrapositive of (3)-(4).
statement:
Assume the conclusion and notation of accepted fact `fdfc3e7459f0e194`. Thus \(A_0,K=A_1,A_2\subset\mathbb R^2\) are nonempty two-dimensional convex polytopes which are sections of one compact polytope,
\[
M=|A_0|>|A_2|=m,\qquad k=|K|,\qquad
t=\frac{2(M+m+k)}9,
\]
and \(f_1,f_2,f_3\) are nonconstant affine functions satisfying
\[
f_1+f_2+f_3=-1.
\]
For \(r\in\{1,2,3\}\), put
\[
c_r=|K\cap\{f_r\leq0\}|,
\]
\[
F_{0r}(a)=|A_0\cap\{f_r\leq a\}|,\qquad
F_{2r}(a)=|A_2\cap\{f_r\leq a\}|,
\]
\[
\mu_r(a)=c_r+F_{0r}(a)+F_{2r}(-a),\qquad
I_r=\{a\in\mathbb R:\mu_r(a)<t\}.
\]
Fix distinct \(i,j,\ell\) with \(\{i,j,\ell\}=\{1,2,3\}\), and suppose
\[
c_j+m<t,\qquad I_i\ne\varnothing,\qquad I_\ell\ne\varnothing.
\tag{1}
\]
Define
\[
\Delta_j=2t-k+c_j.
\tag{2}
\]
Then \(\Delta_j>0\). If \(\Delta_j<m\), then
\[
c_j>\frac14\left(\sqrt M+\sqrt{m-\Delta_j}\right)^2
\tag{3}
\]
and
\[
4mc_j>M(m-\Delta_j).
\tag{4}
\]
Equivalently, under \(c_j+m<t\), if \(\Delta_j<m\) and either
\[
c_j\leq\frac14\left(\sqrt M+\sqrt{m-\Delta_j}\right)^2
\]
or
\[
4mc_j\leq M(m-\Delta_j),
\]
then \(I_i=\varnothing\) or \(I_\ell=\varnothing\).
